_note: DRAFT. Every choice costs something. Effects use the keys documented in tools/sim/sim.js (battery kWh, o2 kg, water kg, food crew-sols, gh_health, gh_growth, cover 0..1, morale, trust, science, risk, fatigue_all, solar {mult, sols}, fault, fix, crew {id: {...}}, sets [flags]). Text is written for ages 7-12.

story.speaker: kenji
story.title: First light at Shoreline
story.text: Morning, Commander. A dust devil rolled over us in the night. The solar panels are dirty, and the air scrubber is making a noise I do not like. I can only fix one today.
story.science: Dust on solar panels is a real problem on Mars. It slowly starved the InSight lander of power.

choices.label: Clean the panels
choices.hint: More power every sol. The scrubber stays noisy and wastes air.
choices.result: Kenji brushes the panels until they shine. Power is up. The scrubber still rattles.

choices.label: Fix the scrubber
choices.hint: The air stays clean. The panels stay dusty and make less power.
choices.result: The rattle stops. The air smells clean. The panels will have to wait.

choices.label: Ask Earth what to do
choices.hint: A wise answer, but it takes a whole day to plan and send. Nothing gets fixed today.
choices.result: Your question races to Earth at the speed of light. It still takes minutes to get there. The answer will come tomorrow.

story.speaker: capcom
story.title: Earth answers
story.text: Shoreline, this is Earth. Good question. Our engineers built a tool overnight. Kenji can do both jobs in half the time. Sorry it took a day. That is how far away you are.
story.science: A radio signal takes between about 4 and 22 minutes to travel one way between Earth and Mars. Rover teams usually plan one whole day at a time.

choices.label: Thanks, Earth
choices.hint: Panels cleaned and scrubber fixed. You lost one day.
choices.result: Both jobs done. Waiting cost you a day, but Earth's idea was a good one.

story.speaker: capcom
story.title: A broken message
story.text: "Shoreline, the lab has looked again at the old rover data from the delta. The spots on that rock are ... [static] ... so when you find it, please ... [static] ... more to follow."
story.science: Big solar flares fill space with radio noise. In May 2024 they caused real radio blackouts on Earth.

choices.label: Keep listening
choices.hint: Power the antenna on the right sols to catch the rest. That power cannot go to anything else.
choices.result: Part 1 of 3 saved. The rest will come when Earth can get a clear signal through.

story.speaker: ana
story.title: Little Sol
story.text: Commander, look! My tomato plant has its first flower. I call her Little Sol. She needs strong light for the next few days or the flower will drop.
story.science: Astronauts have grown lettuce, radishes, chili peppers and dwarf tomatoes on the International Space Station.

choices.label: Promise her the light
choices.hint: Ana is happy. If the greenhouse goes dark before the last sol, she will be heartbroken.
choices.result: Ana grins inside her helmet. "You will not regret it."

choices.label: Say you cannot promise
choices.hint: Honest, but Ana is quiet for the rest of the day.
choices.result: "I understand," Ana says. She waters Little Sol anyway.

story.speaker: kenji
story.title: The last morning
story.text: The ride home lands today. Whatever we did out here, we did it together. Let us count what we are taking back.

choices.label: Begin the last sol
choices.hint: Finish the mission.
choices.result: One more sol.

deck.speaker: kenji
deck.title: A wall of dust
deck.text: There is a dust storm to the west. It will be over us by noon and it will sit here for two sols. The panels will get less than half their light.
deck.science: In 2018 a dust storm covered a quarter of Mars. The sky got so dark that the Opportunity rover could not charge its batteries.

choices.label: Save power and wait
choices.hint: Less than half power for 2 sols. Something has to be switched down.
choices.result: The sky turns the color of weak tea. The battery needle starts to sink.

choices.label: Brush the panels every morning
choices.hint: A bit more power. Two tired people, breathing hard in their suits.
choices.result: Kenji and Zara sweep the panels at dawn. It helps. They come back gray with dust.

deck.speaker: kenji
deck.title: Stale air
deck.text: The scrubber fan has stopped. Without it the air in here slowly fills with the gas we breathe out.
deck.science: Each astronaut breathes out about 1 kilogram of carbon dioxide every day. Machines must scrub it out of the air.

choices.label: Kenji fixes it now
choices.hint: Kenji can do nothing else today.
choices.result: Three hours and one bruised thumb later, the fan spins again.

choices.label: Use the spare canisters
choices.hint: Everyone keeps working. You burn through stored air.
choices.result: The spare canisters hiss. The air is fine, for now. The fan is still broken.

deck.speaker: capcom
deck.title: Waypoint is freezing
deck.text: Shoreline, the supply depot called Waypoint is losing heat. It holds the food and air for the NEXT crew. You are the only ones close enough to send it power.
deck.science: Mars nights can drop to about -153 degrees Celsius. Machines need power just to stay warm.

choices.label: Send Waypoint power
choices.hint: Costs a big piece of your battery. People you will never meet stay safe.
choices.result: Your battery drops. Far away, a little green light comes back on.

choices.label: Keep the power
choices.hint: Your crew is your first job. The next crew may arrive to an empty depot.
choices.result: Nobody says anything at dinner. Zara pushes her food around her plate.

choices.label: Send half
choices.hint: Costs some battery. It may not be enough to save everything.
choices.result: It is something. Waypoint's food freezer holds. Its air tanks do not.

deck.speaker: kenji
deck.title: Drip, drip
deck.text: There is a leak in the water recycler. It is small, but every drop on Mars came a very long way.
deck.science: The International Space Station recycles about 98 percent of its water, including sweat and breath.

choices.label: Patch it today
choices.hint: Kenji is busy all day. You lose a little water.
choices.result: Kenji seals the pipe. "Good as new. Mostly."

choices.label: Put a bucket under it
choices.hint: No work lost today. The leak gets worse every sol until someone fixes it.
choices.result: Plink. Plink. Plink. It is going to be a long night.

deck.speaker: zara
deck.title: A strange rock
deck.text: Commander, the rover camera spotted a pale rock with dark-rimmed spots. It looks like the one in the old pictures. I want one more hour out there.
deck.science: In 2024 the Perseverance rover found a rock in this area, nicknamed Cheyava Falls, with spots scientists call leopard spots. They might be a sign of ancient life, or they might not.

choices.label: Give her the hour
choices.hint: Better science. More rover power and more time far from the shelter.
choices.result: Zara comes back with photographs and a huge smile. "Leopard spots. Just like the old rover saw."

choices.label: Call her back
choices.hint: Safe and on schedule. Zara will not forget it.
choices.result: "Copy," Zara says. Her voice is very flat.

deck.speaker: kenji
deck.title: Kenji's drill
deck.text: I built the storm shelter's air system myself. I have never tried it with all of us inside. Can we practice? It will cost us half a day.
deck.science: NASA plans to protect Mars crews with storm shelters, radiation detectors and space weather forecasts working together.

choices.label: Run the drill
choices.hint: Half a day of work lost. Everyone learns to get to shelter fast.
choices.result: Four people, one tiny room, eleven minutes. "We can do it in five," Kenji says.

choices.label: No time for that
choices.hint: A full day of work. Kenji keeps worrying.
choices.result: Kenji nods and goes back to his tools.

deck.speaker: capcom
deck.title: Letters from home
deck.text: Earth has a bundle of messages from the crew's families. It is a big file. The antenna needs full power to pull it in.
deck.science: Mars missions send their data home through NASA's Deep Space Network, a set of giant dish antennas around the Earth.

choices.label: Download the letters
choices.hint: Costs battery. The crew goes to bed smiling.
choices.result: Ana reads hers three times. Kenji laughs so hard he has to sit down.

choices.label: Not today
choices.hint: Saves power. The messages may be lost in the next burst of solar noise.
choices.result: The file times out. The messages from home never arrive.

deck.speaker: ana
deck.title: One empty tray
deck.text: I have one empty tray and two seed packets. Microgreens are ready to eat in a week. Or I can start a science test that will help every greenhouse after ours.
deck.science: The Canadian Space Agency and NASA both study how to grow fresh food far from Earth, on the Moon and in the far north.

choices.label: Plant microgreens
choices.hint: Fresh food in 6 sols if the lights stay on.
choices.result: Tiny seeds, tiny hopes. "Check back in a week," Ana says.

choices.label: Start the science test
choices.hint: No extra food. Good science.
choices.result: Ana labels forty little pots. "Future farmers will thank us."

deck.speaker: zara
deck.title: A lucky wind
deck.text: A dust devil just danced right across the solar field. It blew the panels clean! It also sandblasted the greenhouse skin.
deck.science: Dust devils really did clean the solar panels of the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, giving them years of extra life.

choices.label: Patch the greenhouse skin
choices.hint: The plants are safe. It uses up the day's spare time.
choices.result: Free power from the wind. The greenhouse gets a few new patches.

choices.label: Enjoy the free power
choices.hint: A full day of work. The plants lose some warmth.
choices.result: The panels sparkle. A few leaves in the greenhouse curl at the edges.

crisis.speaker: zara
crisis.title: Caught in the open
crisis.text: The radiation alarm is screaming. {field_name} is at the delta, far from the shelter, with the sample half out of the ground. There was no warning from Earth. There could not be: the blast came from the far side of the Sun.
crisis.science: On May 20, 2024 the Curiosity rover measured its biggest radiation surge in 12 years. The particles reached Mars only tens of minutes after the eruption.

choices.label: Come home NOW
choices.hint: The rover burns a lot of battery racing back. The sample stays in the ground.
choices.result: The rover throws up a tail of dust all the way home. {field_name} dives through the shelter hatch. The drill is still standing at the delta.

choices.label: Hide under the delta cliff
choices.hint: Rock blocks much of the storm. The sample is saved, but {field_name} is alone out there for a day, using spare air.
choices.result: {field_name} presses into a hollow under 40 meters of ancient river rock, the sample tube held tight.

choices.label: "Your call. I trust you."
choices.hint: If the crew trusts you, they choose well. If not, they chase the sample.

crisis.speaker: kenji
crisis.title: Not enough for both
crisis.text: The shelter's storm mode needs 30 units of battery to keep four people breathing in there all night. We do not have it. I can take the power from the greenhouse, or we make do with less.
crisis.science: Regolith, the loose soil of Mars, can block radiation. A buried room still needs power for air and heat.

choices.label: Greenhouse dark, shelter full
choices.hint: The crew is well protected. The plants sit in the cold and dark.
choices.result: The pink lights go out one row at a time. Ana watches until the last one fades.

choices.label: Both on low power
choices.hint: Plants survive. The shelter gets stuffy and people must step out for air, into the storm.
choices.result: Dim lights in the greenhouse. Thick air in the shelter. Nobody sleeps much.

choices.label: Ana stays with the plants
choices.hint: Shelter at full power for three. Ana keeps the plants alive by hand, behind thin walls.
choices.result: "Go," Ana says. "I have hot water bottles and forty friends in here."

followups.speaker: capcom
followups.title: Too late
followups.text: "Shoreline, Earth. Our far-side spacecraft just saw a huge eruption. We think it is aimed at you. Get to shelter at once. Repeat, at once." The message is dated yesterday.
followups.science: From Earth, nobody could see this flare: it was on the far side of the Sun. A spacecraft called Solar Orbiter later rated it about X12.

choices.label: "Earth, we know. We are still here."
choices.result: Somewhere, 300 million kilometers away, a room full of people is about to cheer.

followups.speaker: ana
followups.title: The quiet greenhouse
followups.text: They are gone, Commander. All of them. Little Sol too. I kept the seeds. Seeds are patient.
followups.science: Plants need light, warmth and water all at once. Take away one for too long and they cannot recover.

choices.label: "I am sorry, Ana."
choices.result: Ana nods. She is already cleaning the trays for next time.

followups.speaker: zara
followups.title: Wait. It went DOWN?
followups.text: Commander, look at the detector. Three solar storms have rolled past us this week and the radiation is LOWER than before. How?
followups.science: A passing solar storm cloud can sweep away some of the cosmic rays that normally rain on Mars. Scientists call it a Forbush decrease. Curiosity measured one in the days before the big storm.

choices.label: "So the alarms were wrong?"
choices.result: "Not wrong," Zara says. "Slow clouds are not the danger. The fast particles are. And those give no warning."
